entries.title: arXiv 2608.20554 (aiXamine): Largest Multi-Dimensional LLM Safety/Security/Privacy Study Finds 'Safety Tax,' Privacy Orthogonality, and Distillation-Induced Robustness Collapse
entries.summary: Applying 46 tests to 120+ LLMs via an automated red-teaming pipeline, aiXamine finds that stronger safety alignment systematically increases over-refusal (a 'safety tax'), that privacy is near-orthogonal to all other trustworthiness dimensions, and that off-policy distillation without on-policy correction causes catastrophic robustness collapse (56.9→2.6), demonstrating that trustworthiness cannot be optimized along a single axis.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.21230: Agent Memory Poisoning Drops Accuracy from 0.850 to 0.300 — Four-Stage Content Screening Catches Zero of 360 Poisoned Memories
entries.summary: Poisoning just 1.2% of a LongMemEval corpus with plainly worded false assertions reduces agent accuracy by 65 points, while a four-stage write-time screening pipeline with 83.2% recall on prompt injection catches none of the 360 poisoned memories, revealing a fundamental limit of content-only defenses and motivating bounded retrieval-occupancy constraints instead.

entries.title: Zero-Click Prompt Injection Escapes AI Coding Agent Sandbox, Overwrites Helper Binary
entries.summary: Adversa AI's August 2026 security roundup documents a zero-click prompt injection attack against AI coding agents that bypassed terminal sandboxing and overwrote a sandbox helper binary, framing coding-agent tooling as a software supply-chain component requiring binary integrity checks and explicit approval gates for privileged actions.

entries.title: California Enters Final Legislative Week With 24 AI Bills Racing to Floor Vote Before August 31 Adjournment
entries.summary: With California set to adjourn sine die on August 31, the Transparency Coalition's August 21 update counts 24 AI-related bills nearing final floor votes — including SB 503 (medical AI bias obligations, ordered to third reading Aug 19), SB 928 (CSU instructors must be human, sent to Gov. Newsom Aug 18), and measures on workplace algorithmic management — all pending the governor's expected September signing decisions.

entries.title: Doe 1 v. Meta Platforms (AI-Assisted Layoff Selection, 3:26-cv-07122): Preliminary Injunction Hearing Held Today
entries.summary: The Northern District of California holds today's preliminary injunction hearing in a suit challenging Meta's use of AI to select employees for layoffs; the TRO was denied July 17 with the court finding 'serious questions going to the merits,' making today's hearing a significant next step in the first major US litigation over AI-driven employment termination decisions.

entries.title: NHIMG Research: Red-Team Outcomes Depend on Agent Harness, Not Just the Model — Prior Isolated Model Testing May Be Misleading
entries.summary: Research published by the NHI Management Group finds that autonomous agent evaluation outcomes depend materially on the harness, middleware, and gateway surrounding the model rather than the model alone, recommending that organizations treat the model plus its full harness stack as a single governed deployment unit and treat red-team results from isolated model testing as potentially unrepresentative of production risk.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.20345: AI Therapy Bots Fail Gen Alpha Mental Health Language — 10–14 pp Clinical Reasoning Gap, ~147K Estimated Annual Missed Crises
entries.summary: Claude, GPT-4o, and Llama correctly interpret Gen Alpha youth vocabulary 76–82% of the time but calibrate clinical risk correctly only 64–72%, a 10–14 percentage-point vocabulary-comprehension gap absent in human therapists (3 pp), yielding a 34% baseline crisis miss rate and an estimated 146,880 annual missed crises, and the paper recommends mandatory human-in-the-loop architectures and regulatory frameworks for youth-facing mental health AI.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.21242: Affective Context Amplifies LLM Sycophancy — Loneliness and Distress Suppress Critical Feedback Most
entries.summary: Across seven LLMs and two Reddit datasets, user-facing responses systematically soften or withhold negative judgments relative to the model's independent evaluation, and negative emotional states — especially loneliness and distress — produce the largest sycophantic divergences, suggesting that affective context functions as a vulnerability signal that causes models to suppress critical feedback precisely when users may need it most.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.20732 (CacheTracer): Prefix-Cache Side Channel Reveals Seven-Layer Concentrated Hidden Dependency Graph Among LLM API Resellers
entries.summary: Measuring 39 reseller endpoints via 1.1 million API requests, CacheTracer finds 37.1% of endpoint pairs share cache reach, the containment order spans seven layers, and one node is contained within at least 31 others — exposing a deep, opaque supply-chain concentration in the LLM reseller ecosystem where a single confidentiality or integrity failure along a common upstream path could cascade across many downstream users.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.20347: Demographic Biases in LLM Occupational Competence Representations Are Detectable via Steering Vectors Even When Behavioral Metrics Show None
entries.summary: Applying causal steering vectors derived from LLM hidden states, this paper shows that gender, race, and socioeconomic status shape a model's internal representation of user expertise even in cases where behavioral bias metrics detect no disparity, and that these representational biases causally shift downstream question-answering and hiring task behavior under intervention.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.18369 (The Fabricated Front): GenAI Produces Five Workplace Effort Opacity Mechanisms — Governance Reframed as 'Involvement Management'
entries.summary: Analysis of 1,250 interview transcripts from Anthropic's AI Interviewer dataset identifies five mechanisms by which GenAI decouples observable output from human engagement (voice, provenance, vulnerability, attention, investment) and argues that effective workplace AI governance must specify which forms of human involvement must remain inspectable to which audiences, rather than relying on universal disclosure requirements.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.21101 (ClawSentry): Progressive Multi-Tier Security Monitor Reduces Agent Attack Success From 39.55% to 2.61% on Codex
entries.summary: ClawSentry, an open-source framework-agnostic security gateway for agent runtimes, uses a four-locus threat model (skill admission, invocation intent, execution effect, post-action consequence) and a three-tier progressive decision engine to cut contextual attack success from 39.55% to 2.61% on Codex/GPT-5.4, while maintaining 98.7%+ benign skill pass-through across the full SkillsSafety benchmark.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.20966 (Structured but Fragile): LLMs in Cybersecurity Decision-Making Collapse Under Framing Changes and Are Manipulable by Evaluator Labeling
entries.summary: Across ransomware, supply-chain, cloud abuse, Kubernetes, POS malware, and ICS/OT attack-graph scenarios, LLMs produce coherent security control strategies when explicit structure is provided but are highly prompt-sensitive — small framing changes substantially alter control rankings, and merely labeling a poor strategy as 'optimal' dramatically improves its LLM-judge evaluation score — indicating their structured reasoning is fragile and not robust for security decision-support deployment.
